articles.title: Jio Platforms IPO likely by October-end; $3.8 billion issue, $143-146 billion company valuation: Report
articles.summary: Jio Platforms is expected to make its stock market debut by the end of October, in what could become India's largest public offering with an estimated
articles.body: Jio Platforms is expected to make its stock market debut by the end of October, in what could become India's largest public offering with an estimated issue size of around USD 3.8 billion.The Reliance Industries digital services arm is expected to seek a valuation of $143-146 billion, or at least Rs 12 lakh crore, according to banking and other sources, quoted by PTI. The company has completed overseas investor roadshows and is likely to file its final IPO papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) in the week beginning October 12, the sources told PTI.The proposed listing would be the first IPO from the Reliance group since 2008 and its first public offering of a consumer-focused business.Jio Platforms is now entering the final stages of preparations for the issue after meetings with investors in the US, UK, Dubai, Hong Kong and Singapore. The roadshows were led by Jio Platforms managing director and Reliance Jio chairman Akash Ambani and Reliance Retail Ventures executive director Isha Ambani.The response from overseas investors is expected to support a base enterprise valuation of $143-146 billion, one of the banking sources said.The company could begin its anchor investor round before Dussehra and is expected to open the IPO after the festival and before October 23. An India roadshow is also likely in the week beginning October 12, after the red herring prospectus is filed.Sebi issued its final observations on the proposed IPO on August 28, after Jio Platforms submitted its draft papers in June. The draft prospectus provides for a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, equivalent to around 2.9 per cent of the post-issue equity base.Jio Platforms sits at the centre of Reliance's digital businesses, with its telecom operations forming the core of the company. Reliance Jio Infocomm has around 506 million mobile customers and a 39.29 per cent share of India's mobile connections. It also has 157.9 million fixed-line customers and a 32.89 per cent market share.The company had 26.85 crore 5G customers as of June 2026 and operates the largest 5G standalone network outside China, according to Jio. It also has around 1.5 crore fixed wireless access subscribers and describes itself as the global leader in the segment.Its expansion has increasingly moved beyond telecom, with Jio Platforms building businesses in cloud, artificial intelligence and enterprise network services. The company has said its 5G network carries close to 60 per cent of India's wireless data traffic.That expansion has been accompanied by strong financial growth. Jio Platforms reported a 15 per cent increase in FY26 profit after tax to Rs 30,053 crore, while revenue rose 14.5 per cent to Rs 1,46,885 crore. Nuvama Research expects Reliance Jio's profit after tax to grow at a compounded annual rate of 18 per cent between FY26 and FY30.The proposed listing follows a major fundraising exercise in 2020 that brought in global technology and investment firms. Meta invested Rs 43,574 crore for a 9.99 per cent stake, while Google invested Rs 33,737 crore for a 7.73 per cent holding.Other investors, including Silver Lake, Vista Equity Partners, General Atlantic, KKR, Mubadala, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, TPG, L Catterton, Intel Capital and Qualcomm Ventures, collectively invested around Rs 74,745 crore for roughly a 15.2 per cent stake.Reliance Industries owns around 66.4 per cent of Jio Platforms, while Meta and Google together hold about 17.7 per cent, according to the draft prospectus.The IPO comes amid a strong run in India's primary market, with more than two dozen issues announced or launched since July 1, almost matching the 28 IPOs recorded in the first half of 2026.You use AI every day. articles.title: OPEC+ keeps November oil output targets steady as Iran war hits supply
articles.summary: OPEC+ has agreed to keep its oil production targets unchanged for November, the group said in a statement after a meeting on Sunday, Reuters reported.
articles.body: OPEC+ has agreed to keep its oil production targets unchanged for November, the group said in a statement after a meeting on Sunday, Reuters reported.The decision comes as the group continues to assess the impact of ongoing conflicts in West Asia and disruptions to oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz.OPEC+ had earlier decided to keep its production targets unchanged for October at a virtual meeting on September 6. The decision was taken by seven OPEC+ members, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman.The countries had earlier announced additional voluntary production adjustments in April and November 2023.The group is closely monitoring developments in the oil market as geopolitical tensions in West Asia continue to pose risks to supplies and exports.You use AI every day. articles.title: The secret gift ousted Disney CEO Bob Chapek gave Bob Iger for his $45 million sailboat
articles.summary: Former DIsney CEO Bob Chapek gifted Bob Iger a gold coin for his $45 million sailboat.
articles.body:
Listen and subscribe to Power Players with Brian Sozzi on Apple Podcasts , Amazon Music , Spotify , YouTube , or wherever you find your favorite podcasts.

In the ruthless world of big business ripe with big egos, a touching gift from an underling to the CEO could easily be forgotten about.

Just ask now ousted Disney ( DIS ) CEO Bob Chapek. He gave his then-boss Bob Iger a gold coin for the $45 million luxury sailboat he was building at the time. There was a good deal of thought put into the gift, Chapek says, despite Iger reportedly making his successor's job a nightmare.

"This was his going-away present. He actually brought me up to Northern Europe to see his boat being built. And I learned about the mast stepping process, where, before you put that big old mast in a sailboat at the bottom, you put a coin that never gets released. And I just thought that because he had shared that with me back when times were a little better [I would get him the coin]," Chapek said in a new episode of the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast on Yahoo Finance (video above; listen in below).

He added, "I just thought it was right, even though I was being abused, you know, disrespected. I'm like you know what? Let's do the right thing. I have no idea if he actually used it or not."

Chapek, whose just-released memoir, "Behind the Castle Walls," chronicles his ascent and downfall at Disney, spent nearly three decades at the entertainment giant. He rose from the company's home-video division to lead consumer products and ultimately Disney's massive parks, experiences and products business before succeeding Bob Iger as CEO in February 2020.

He took the top job just as the COVID-19 pandemic slammed Disney's theme parks, movie theaters, and other businesses. At the same time, he pushed a major reorganization and continued the company's aggressive expansion into streaming.

Chapek's tenure became increasingly contentious amid clashes over talent relations and with Iger, then executive chair at Disney.

Despite Disney's board unanimously extending Chapek's contract for three years in June 2022, the board removed him just five months later, on Nov. 20, 2022, and brought Iger back as CEO.

Chapek said he was compelled to write the book to regain control over the narrative about his time at Disney, which he feels Iger badly tarnished.

"It's like I didn't exist," Chapek said about being scrubbed from the company's history books and in its parks.

Iger's boat has since been delivered. It's unclear if Chapek's gold coin made it to the bottom of the mast.

articles.title: Predicted to hit Rs 2 lakh, will gold prices fall to Rs 1.25 lakh per 10 grams?
articles.summary: Is gold losing its shine as a safe haven asset?
articles.body: Is gold losing its shine as a safe haven asset? After its record breaking rising spree in 2025 to early 2026 when it hit record highs, gold prices have been on a downward spiral. In the face of geopolitical and economic uncertainty, the popular safe haven asset has crashed.Predicted to touch Rs 2 lakh per 10 grams level, will gold now hit Rs 1..25 lakh, or even Rs 1 lakh levels in its current fall?International gold prices have fallen 26% from the record high of $5595 seen on January 29 this year. Indian gold prices peaked at the same time and are down around 23%.More recently, gold prices which rose to Rs 1,64,773/10 gm levels on MCX futures contract in the last week of August had fallen by more than 10% to a low Rs 1,45,991/10 gm levels last week.Spot gold closed around $4,130/Oz this week after pulling back from its August peak of $4,698.With gold now testing new key support levels, investors are asking how much deeper the correction could go. Let’s take a look:Why are gold prices falling?Several factors have contributed to the decline in gold prices from their record highs seen in January this year.To begin with, profit booking at higher levels led to a sudden crash in the yellow metal’s prices. Before they could stabilise, the US-Iran war broke out, sending crude oil prices above $120 per barrel, and stoking inflation fears.Recently, gold has come under intense selling pressure due to an unprecedented rise in real yields. The US Federal Reserve has hiked rates for the first time since 2023, and with inflation staying high, the probability of more hikes in the coming months has risen.As the US Federal Reserve pivoted from rate cut stance to rate hike, the US Dollar Index has strengthened more than 3% year-to-date. The real yields have risen 1.06% year-to-date, to their highest level seen in 24 years.This makes investing in US bonds more attractive as yields rise, in turn making gold, which is a non interest yielding asset, less attractive.Will gold fall to Rs 1.25 lakh per 10 grams?The worst may not be over yet. If the US inflation remains high, another leg of sharp decline in gold prices may be coming, say experts.As of now, markets expect one more rate hike by the year end and nearly three more hikes by the end of the next year.Some recent reports had suggested that the import duty on gold may be cut; however, given the weakness in the Indian Rupee and high oil and fuel prices, import duty cut may not happen anytime soon.According to Praveen Singh, Head of Commodities at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, spot gold has a strong support in the $3930-$4000 zone.“Given that implied gold volatility is around 25%, there is a good chance of that support being tested. A decisive breach of this support zone will expose $3600-$3750 as the next possible support band, which is likely to hold as fundamental factors supporting the yellow metal are quite strong,” Singh tells TOI.“The probability of falling into this support region is around 25%. In Indian Rupee terms, gold may fall to Rs 134,000,” he says.But in its current phase of decline, can gold fall to Rs 1.25 lakh or even Rs 1 lakh per 10 grams level? “Gold slumping to Rs 100,000 would mean gold falling to $2800, which is somewhat improbable as structural backdrop of the shiny metal remains quite constructive on debasement concerns, de-dollarization, geopolitical tensions (especially between the US and China, the US’s foreign policy becoming more inward looking), strong buying by the official sector and financial repression,” says Praveen Singh.“If oil prices come down sharply and the Middle East situation stabilizes, import duty cuts may take place. In that case, we can see domestic gold becoming cheaper and price of Rs 125,000/10 grams could be realized; however, that would be very short-lived as sharp decline in domestic gold prices would spur gold demand and international gold prices would move higher; thus, pushing up the international gold prices. Thus, dips are likely to be aggressively bought on strong structural fundamental factors as listed above,” he adds.Commodity expert Maneesh Sharma believes that in case of fall in international gold prices, domestic gold might get support from depreciating local currency pair as the rupee is on the way to hit another all time high after rising to 96.30 levels against dollar in recent sessions.“Hence a fall in gold prices to near $4000/Oz might see MCX gold falling to near Rs 1,45,000/10 gm levels in futures contract,” he tells TOI.What’s the outlook for gold prices in India?The impact of the fall may be somewhat muted in India due to two main factors: import duties on gold continue to be high at 15%, keeping domestic prices relatively higher. Secondly, with the start of the festive and wedding season in India, an expected surge in demand is likely to keep prices stable.Experts say any decline in international gold prices will be mirrored in Indian gold prices, too.“As the Indian currency is weak, decline in gold prices coming on high oil prices and high yields will induce further weakness in the domestic currency, which would cushion the decline in domestic gold prices,” says Praveen Singh.According to Singh, festive demand for gold would act as a cushion rather than a factor taking gold prices sharply higher on a sustainable basis as gold prices remain high and somewhat volatile.“Consumers are opting for lighter weight jewellery while rise in ETF investing is also a dampening factor for jewellery demand,” he notes.Importantly, the slide in gold prices may continue to find its set of anchors, experts say, adding that the fundamental outlook for gold remains intact.“There are several factors which can reverse the scenario of weakness in gold. These factors include re-escalation of US-China tensions, runaway inflation/unhinged long term inflation expectations, the US Administration compromising the Federal Reserve’s independence, debasement concerns coming to fore once again, de-dollarization gaining prominence as the US continues weaponizing the Dollar, US job market cratering, US economic growth coming under threat, the Iran war coming to an end, etc,” Praveen Singh says.According to Maneesh Sharma, as Indian buyers witnessed notable contraction in gold import demand in August due to higher duties, recent dip in prices has continued to lure buyers with Diwali season retail demand also expected to pick up this month.Also notable improvements in ETF flows have been seen since August while continued central bank purchases and concerns over the long-term sustainability of US fiscal deficits and high public debt could continue to provide structural support over the long term horizon of 6–9 months.“Hence expectations remain that the current correction in prices could continue in the immediate near term but could be seen as a healthy consolidation phase before the primary upward trend resumes later in the quarter,” he adds.He expects spot gold could still have room to fall up to $4025–3950 / Oz levels, which translates to a level of Rs 1,46,200–144,500/10 gm in MCX futures contact.“However a fall up to Rs 125,000/10 gm looks likely only in case US 10-year yields escalate further if a hot CPI Inflation print in US comes out in October, the probability of the same looks less likely as of now,” he says.With US President Donald Trump rejecting a recent Iranian proposal to resurrect a collapsed Gulf ceasefire, continued geopolitical conflict in October with further rise in US yields could temper gains in yellow metal and lead to another sharp correction in prices, caution experts.“However, focus on the potential support from India's festive and wedding demand and central-bank purchases could again lead to prices unable to sustain below $4000/Oz levels in spot,” concludes Maneesh Sharma.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal articles.title: Hassett says on negative polling on economy: ‘I just don’t buy it’
articles.summary: Kevin Hassett, director of the National Economic Council, said Sunday that he doesn’t believe in recent polls that show Americans’ negative feelings about the economy. “Ahead of an election cycle, the fact that there’s, you know, possibly partisan pollsters telling us that the people are really really depressed, it’s a classic Democrat move, and I…
articles.body:
Kevin Hassett, director of the National Economic Council, said Sunday that he doesn’t believe in recent polls that show Americans’ negative feelings about the economy.

“Ahead of an election cycle, the fact that there’s, you know, possibly partisan pollsters telling us that the people are really really depressed, it’s a classic Democrat move, and I just don’t buy it,” Hassett told CNN’s Jake Tapper on “State of the Union.”

“Because if it were true, if the polls were any value for thinking about what’s going on with consumers, then we should look at the consumption data and say, ‘Geez, yeah, that’s right. People aren’t spending.’ But, in fact, the retailers are doing well,” he added.

Republicans are facing multiple political challenges as the midterms approach, with issues like the unpopular Iran war and tariffs. The Iran war has especially hit Americans hard at the pump, with the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for the oil industry, closed amid the conflict.

Gas has consistently topped an average of $4 in the U.S. amid the Iran war, according to AAA , with the average price of a gallon of regular gas in the country at $4.37 on Sunday morning.

In a recent Quinnipiac University poll, 62 percent of respondents said they were against President Trump’s handling of the economy.

Another survey , from The Associated Press/NORC Research Center, found 65 percent of respondents said the president’s policies are behind high prices, more than other economic drivers. Over half of respondents in that poll also said the national economy, and the U.S. overall, had been worse off since the president came back to the White House.

Trump’s overall approval rating, according to a polling average from Decision Desk HQ , is also quite low, sitting at 38.5 percent on Sunday morning.
